gaps: Records with "to": null were still in office on 2026-09-25 (Legislature dissolved 2026-09-22; ministers remain in office).

LLBC lists exclude acting appointments. Acting holders recorded here come only from secondary sources: Murray Rankin (acting Attorney General and Minister Responsible for Housing, 2022-07-19 to 2022-08-02, per LLBC footnote citing OIC 596/2020); Brenda Bailey (acting Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills, 2024-02-05 to 2024-02-20, per Wikipedia); Adrian Dix (covering Jobs and Economic Growth while Bailey is on leave; the release says her treatment begins late August 2026 and she expects to return early October 2026, so exact dates are unknown). Other short acting or 'first acting minister' coverings (e.g., during absences) were not found.

Horgan-appointed ministers stayed in office under Premier Eby from 2022-11-18 until Eby's cabinet was sworn in 2022-12-07. Following LLBC, their records end 2022-12-07 but carry premier 'John Horgan' (Wikipedia ends them 2022-11-18). Ministers who were reappointed to the same portfolio on 2022-12-07 (Bains, Beare, Dean, Dix, Farnworth, Fleming, Heyman, Rankin) are split into a Horgan record and an Eby record.
Minister of Public Safety and Solicitor General was vacant 2012-02-08 to 2015-12-11; those responsibilities sat with the Minister of Justice and Attorney General.

Attorney General styling: LLBC lists 'Attorney General' and 'Justice' separately; the combined title 'Minister of Justice and Attorney General' is used here from 2012-02-08 (the LLBC 'Justice' start date) to 2017-07-18. Wikipedia gives 2012-02-02 for the change.
Rename-date disagreement: Wikipedia says Agriculture, Food and Fisheries became Agriculture and Food on 2022-03-01; LLBC (used here) says 2022-04-01.

Wikipedia's Eby ministry table lists Brenda Bailey's 2026-08-14 appointment as 'Jobs, Economic Development and Innovation'. The BC Gov News release (used here) styles it 'Minister of Jobs and Economic Growth'.

Deliberately omitted: Premier and Deputy Premier (no departments); ministers of state (e.g., Child Care, Trade, Infrastructure, Emergency Preparedness, Seniors, Small Business, Tourism and Small Business, Multiculturalism, Rural Economic Development, Lands and NRO, Workforce Development, Sustainable Forestry Innovation, Infrastructure and Transit, Local Governments and Rural Communities, Community Safety, AI and New Technologies); ministers without portfolio (Melanie Mark 2022-09-28 to 2023-04-14, Grace Lore from 2024-12-10); and minor 'Minister Responsible for' add-ons (Multiculturalism, Asia Pacific Strategy, Core Review, Accessibility, Liquor Distribution Branch, TransLink, Consular Corps, Francophone Affairs, Columbia Basin Trust). Housing, Labour (2012–2017) and Fisheries (2022) 'Minister Responsible for' roles are kept because they carried departmental functions.
Names follow LLBC (e.g., 'Michael de Jong', 'Michael Morris', better known as Mike). The exception is Jessie Sunner: LLBC spells it 'Jessi' in one list and 'Jessie' in the other.
